narr: In a seasonably very unstable airmass south of a frontal boundary and ahead of an approaching upper level shortwave, scattered storms developed across central Mississippi in the early morning. In the presence of robust mid-level wind shear, these storms rapidly became severe and produced several instances of hail as large as 1.5 inches. A break in severe thunderstorm activity was noted from mid morning into mid afternoon when diurnal building instability fostered redevelopment of robust and severe thunderstorm activity. Storms in the afternoon into the evening would prove to be substantially more intense, with numerous reports of downed trees and hail as large as 2.75 inches, or approximately baseball size. Numerous rounds of strong to severe storms would also contribute to instances of flash flooding in the area. This activity was focused along the interstate-20 corridor where the most intense storm damage was noted with impacts that also extended into southern portions of the state. The activity would persist into the evening before diminishing.
